name: Planner
description: A plan of tasks and milestones for your projects as a Gantt chart, a board or a list. Agents validate, reschedule and give feedback through actions whose prompts you edit, and tasks can follow GitHub issues, boards and pull requests.

permissions.reason: To run actions in the project a task belongs to and find the project of a repository.
To follow the pull requests linked to a task and mark it done when they merge.
To turn the issues, milestones and board of the repositories you follow into tasks.
With two-way sync, to send changes to a task back to its issue and board, and to create issues for tasks.
To know the project of a thread whose agent works on a task.
Each action, and each piece of work on a task, is a thread of the agent you chose.
Agents read the plan and report their proposals and progress through tools of this plugin.
To hear replies to the status updates it posts and the slash command.
To post status updates and waiting proposals to the plan's channel, and answer the slash command.

settings.label: Agent
settings.description: The provider instance that runs actions, such as claudeAgent or codex.

settings.label: Model
settings.description: Empty for the agent's default model.

settings.label: Access for actions
settings.description: Actions read the plan and the project and report back; they rarely need more.

settings.label: Access for work on a task
settings.description: Work on a task happens in a worktree of its own.

settings.label: Default project
settings.description: Where actions on tasks with no project, and actions on the whole plan, run.

settings.label: Show planner threads
settings.description: On the Planner page only, its threads stay out of the thread list.

settings.label: Actions

validate.label: Validate progress

reschedule.label: Reschedule

feedback.label: Give feedback

breakdown.label: Break down

status.label: Write status update

work.label: Start work

settings.description: Each action's label, whether it acts on one task or the whole plan, and its prompt. {{today}}, {{plan}}, {{items}}, {{project}} and {{item.title}}, {{item.notes}}, {{item.status}}, {{item.start}}, {{item.due}}, {{item.progress}}, {{item.owner}}, {{item.labels}}, {{item.issue}}, {{item.pullRequests}}, {{item.subtasks}} and {{item.after}} are filled in. How to report is added after it.

settings.label: Let every thread read the plan
settings.description: Agents in any thread can read the plan. Only planner threads can change it.

settings.label: Repositories
settings.description: owner/name of each repository whose issues become tasks. Each needs a project on this MC.

settings.label: Only issues labelled
settings.description: Empty to follow every open issue.

settings.label: GitHub sync
settings.description: Both ways sends changes to a task back to its issue and board.

settings.label: GitHub Project
settings.description: owner/number of a GitHub Project whose date fields are the tasks' dates. Needs gh's project scope.

settings.label: Done when its pull requests merge
Post to Slack channel
settings.description: A channel the MC's Slack bot is in, as #name or its id. Empty for no Slack.

settings.label: Slash command
settings.description: Add it to your Slack app to ask for the plan's status or run an action from Slack.
